MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: __8___
  Meeting Date: May 22, 2018

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

FROM:  SHERI REPP-LOADSMAN, DEPUTY CITY MANAGER/PLANNING &
  BUILDING DIRECTOR /s/

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS
  OF MAY 10, 2018

DATE:  MAY 22, 2018

ISSUE/PURPOSE

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendations from
the May 10, 2018 meeting to the City Council.

BACKGROUND/DISCUSSION

At its meeting of May 10, 2018, the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed seven
applications for tree removals.

A. PC-488-18; Application to remove 2 Canary Island pine trees located in the parkway
  adjacent to 1609 Via Zurita

Applicant: Yelena and Boris Gelman
  1608 Via Zurita
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application and recommended additional conditions to address the
concern that a portion of one or both of the subject trees might be located on public property.
Staff advised that the trunks of the trees appeared to be fully within public property and the

  Page 1 of 5

  001
 proposed conditions would require a survey and final determination. Mr. Wang, owner of 1609
Via Zurita, questioned if a decision should be made before a survey is completed. Mr.
Fitzgerald questioned slope stability if trees to be removed and Mr. Acosta requested the trees
not be removed. The Parklands Committee considered the testimony and determined that the
trees appeared to be public and a substantial view impairment exists as a result of the trees.

Action: Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-488-18 with conditions as follows:

1. Require the Standard Conditions for tree removal approvals.
2. Require payment of $1,000 to the Tree Bank.
3. Require removal of the stumps.
4. Prior to issuance of any permit for a tree removal, the applicant shall submit a survey to
  determine the location of the two Canary Island pine trees located adjacent to 1609 Via Zurita.
5. Such survey shall be reviewed by the City to determine that the subject tree trunks are located
  within the public right-of-way and are properly characterized as public trees.
6. If in the sole determination of the City, the tree trunks are determined to be partially located
  on private property, the City shall require the applicant to obtain authorization for the tree
  removals through the Palos Verdes Homes Association pursuant to adopted guidelines and
  established procedures for implementing the view restoration consistent with the enabling
  covenants, conditions and restrictions. Issuance of any permit for a tree removal shall be
  contingent upon any and all requirements of the Palos Verdes Homes Association having been
  satisfied, including but not limited to any legal proceedings by Alternate Dispute Resolution
  and a court action.

The vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

B. PC-501-18; Application to remove 2 Eucalyptus trees located in the parkway adjacent to
  2601 Via Olivera

Applicant: Francis Kupieu
  2560 Via Olivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application. Mr. Kupieu noted Eucalyptus tree not the designated tree and
views have been blocked by 50% as a result of the trees. Mr. Simon requested the trees be
trimmed to maintain privacy and habitat for birds.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-501-18. Recommend removal of the smaller Eucalyptus and approval
to trim the Silver Dollar Eucalyptus to lower and thin the density to improve the view and
maintain the health of the tree. Authorization to remove one tree is according to the ‘Standard
Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals’. Payment of $500 to the Tree Bank and removal of
the stump are required. The vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

  Page 2 of 5

  002
 C. PC-502-18; Application to remove 1 Canary Island Date palm located on the Nogales Path
  adjacent to 941 Via Nogales

Applicant: Norman MacKnight
  405 Via Chico #11
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this as a request to remove one Canary Island Date palm. There was no
testimony on this item.

Action: Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
Council denial of PC-502-18. Recommend approval to trim the Canary Island palm to remove
the lower fronds to a configuration of 9 and 3 on the face of a clock. The vote was (3-0-2 in
favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

D. PC-504-18; Application to remove 1 Eucalyptus tree located in the parkway adjacent to
  1641 Via Lazo

Applicant: Dwight Streit
  1641 Via Lazo
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

The application requested approval to remove a Eucalyptus tree. Mr. Haggerty testified that
the tree had grown into the view and requested removal. The applicant noted that several
neighbors had requested he remove the tree and requested that the tree be replaced with a better
tree. Ms. Nunnery noted appreciation for applicant and stated neighbors had chipped in.

Action: Committee member Leach motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-504-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
Approvals’. Payment of $500 to the Tree Bank and removal of the stump are required. The
vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

E. PC-505-18; Application to remove 1 Stone pine tree located in the parkway adjacent to
  2546 Palos Verdes Drive West and trim or remove 2 Ficus trees and 1 Aleppo pine tree
  located in the center median between Avenida Mirola and Via Zumaya

Applicant: Robert Green
  2537 Via Rivera
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application. Mr. Green advised that Stone pine tree was lifting driveway
and other trees blocking view. Mr. David supported restoration of views. Ms. Breene
recommended different type of trimming to allow for view enhancement, noting more assertive
trimming could lead to less tree removals. Ms. Gasco stated the trees were important to the
community and should be retained. Ms. Paparo also noted the importance of the trees for
shading, noise reduction and habitat. Ms. Ickes advised trees were blocking views. Mr.
Hamilton reiterated importance of trees and requested all be preserved.

  Page 3 of 5

  003
 Action: Committee member Kaviani motioned second by Leach to recommend to the City
Council deny PC-505-18. Approve trimming of the trees on a regular schedule by the applicant
with a permit from the City.

The vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

F. PC-506-18; Application to remove 1 Canary Island Date palm tree located in the parkway
  adjacent to 868 Via Del Monte

Applicant: Jerry Donahue
  864 Rincon Lane
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to remove one Canary Island Date palm due to
view obstruction. The applicant stated his opinion that the tree was a volunteer and not
compatible with the parklands. Dr. Mitral requested another tree be planted to help shield lights
and provide a protective barrier, noting the tree has stopped several cars from coming off the
road. Mr. Larson noted the view obstruction for his development site.

Action: Committee member Leach motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-506-18; according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
Approvals’. Require $500 payment to the ‘Tree Bank’ and surface grinding of the stump only.
Provide a new tree to be planted by the City subject to approval by the Urban Forester. The
vote was (2-1-2 in favor, Richie-Bray dissenting, Wade and Rubincam absent).

G. PC-507-18; Application to remove 2 Red Iron Bark Eucalyptus trees located in the
  parkways adjacent to 736 and 741 Cloyden Road

Applicant: Irv Miller
  745 Cloyden Road
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to remove two Red Iron Eucalyptus trees. The
applicant noted there were 13 of these tree, 9 being close together. He stated that removal
would not impact neighborhood character. Mrs. Helmy stated her support.

Action: Committee member Leach motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the City
Council approval of PC-507-18 according to the ‘Standard Conditions for Tree Removal
Approvals’. Payment of $1,000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal of the stumps are required. The
vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

  Page 4 of 5

  004
 H. PC-508-18; Application to remove 1 Canary Island Date palm tree and 1 Eucalyptus tree
  located in the parkway adjacent to 2548 Via Carrillo

Applicant: Vicki Hulbert
  1040 Via Palestra
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a request to remove two trees. The applicant stated she was
representing the entire neighborhood and that the trees should be removed for safety. She
asked if the palm tree could be authorized for relocation. Staff noted that authorization for
removal did not mean that the tree had to be cut down and that relocation could be an
alternative.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Kaviani to recommend to the
City Council approval of PC-508-18, with modification, to deny removal of the Eucalyptus
tree and authorize removal of the Canary Island Date palm tree according to the ‘Standard
Conditions for Tree Removal Approvals’. Payment of $1,000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and removal
of the stumps are required. The vote was (3-0-2 in favor, Wade and Rubincam absent).

NOTIFICATION

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above
noted recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in
the standard manner for City Council meetings.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council take the following actions:

1. Review and approve the Parklands Committee Recommended Actions of May 10, 2018.
